# Revised radio geometry: complete tables

Orbital-component diagnostics only; former beam crossing/position accuracy claims withdrawn. arctan2(abs(orbital component), mean altitude); not a full topocentric error or sky-track displacement. abs(in_track_km)/circular_orbit_speed_km_s; not a beam timing residual.
An orbital-component threshold failure at the first sampled age leaves fresher ages unmeasured. It does not establish a beam-crossing failure, a whole receiver-band limit or the impossibility of a radio observation.

The primary scalar criterion uses a width fraction of 0.333333 and an empirical inside fraction of 95.0%. The alternate criterion and maximum-width choices are descriptive sensitivities; the nominal analytic comparison is explicitly historical.

Beam source: [de Villiers, MeerKAT Holography Measurements in the UHF, L, and S bands](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.06752); data: [MeerKAT measured primary-beam data release](https://doi.org/10.48479/wdb0-h061).

The topocentric comparison admits 112/10310 source-filtered set/lead trials and constructs 18144 beam/pointing/observation cases. Those eligible curves come from 94 element sets on 12 spacecraft. Eligibility: nominal elevation at target 15 through 85 degrees; entire ±180 s curves finite with reference coverage and zero SGP4 codes. Geometry: complete TEME positions transformed with IERS UT1/polar motion, rotating WGS84 observer, fixed ICRS boresight; no refraction. Pointings: fixed ICRS centre and signed normal offsets, each sign scaled to its first measured half-power boundary. These are previously inspected evaluation windows and constructed pointings, not an untouched test population or an observing schedule. The source frequencies below are the actual measured frequency slices. Cases sharing a trajectory are correlated.

Eligibility inventory: nominal_below_horizon: 9829; nominal_below_15_degrees: 369; eligible: 112.

The declared offsets at -1, 1 half-power radii are deliberate boundary stress cases. Their classification counts remain in the full inventory and are shown separately from the other declared offsets. Removing these exact-radius constructions is a descriptive sensitivity, not a new test population. The numerical near-threshold diagnostic is separate from this construction-based split.

Across the full-span constructed cases, absolute closest-time error has median 0.0586055 s, interpolated 95.0% quantile 1.39157 s and maximum 12.5531 s (n=6048). Prediction/reference closest-time censoring counts are 0/0. Instantaneous line-of-sight separation at reference closest approach has absolute median 0.0150169 deg, interpolated 95.0% quantile 0.364757 deg and maximum 3.51611 deg (n=6048). These are repeated geometric comparisons on the eligible curves, not independent timing trials. Range-rate, interferometric coherence and received power have not been validated by this beam-geometry experiment.

uncensored paired closest times; entry/exit only for both observation crossings and one uncensored full-span interval each. descriptive clustered cases; no independent-trial confidence or population guarantee. No scalar component horizon is promoted to a general beam or observing guarantee.

Near-boundary means absolute peak-minus-half-power margin at most 1e-8, matching the scorer's tangency tolerance. This flags classification sensitivity even when a tiny interval is reported. Frozen classifications are retained.

The pre-run protocol copies old window registry notes verbatim. Their held-out wording is historical metadata, not evidence of untouched v2 evaluation data.
